## Welcome {.unnumbered}

::: {.column-margin}
![**The Physical AI Stack**. In digital software, execution stops at the silicon chip. In physical AI, execution ends with irreversible physical contact. To safely bridge high-latency foundation models (The Brain) to real-world physics (The Boundary), we must introduce hard real-time safety enforcement (The Body) connected by deterministic lock-free communications (The Nervous System).](/vol4/parts/images/stack_vol4.svg){#fig-vol4-stack width=100%}
:::

**This is an active draft.** Physical AI systems begin where computation stops being symbolic and becomes physical force. Once an algorithm commands a motor, the forgiving conventions of digital software give way to mechanics, thermodynamics, and actions that cannot be undone.

## What You Will Learn {.unnumbered}

The book progresses through four parts:

- **The Machine Anatomy** develops the causal boundary, the body, the nervous system, and the brain, establishing where computation acquires physical consequence.
- **Teaching the Machine** develops data, training, and evaluation for systems whose own actions determine what they observe next.
- **Running the Machine** develops perception, memory, intent, planning, enforcement, and placement across the timescales that separate deliberation from motor control.
- **Governing the Machine** develops intervention, verification, release, and the open frontier, covering what dependability requires once a machine leaves the laboratory.

:::
